entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 rotation-A global map of 2025-08-29
entries.finding: The body map is the archive's 1,800 by 900 F395N/F502N/F631N composite, resampled with a Lanczos-3 kernel to the 2,880 by 1,440 grid and retained byte-identical under the package's observations directory, with the declared solar color applied in linear light.

entries.subject: The visible body image at 4,096 by 2,048
entries.finding: The body image is 2,048 by 1,024 texels from a 1,800 by 900 source; Jupiter's source is 3,600 by 1,800. At the default view on a 2x screen one Saturn source pixel covers 1.8 screen pixels (disc radius 511 px), one of Jupiter's 0.9. A 4,096 by 2,048 image prepared from the same source held 4 % more fine detail than the shipped size in a composed flood-lit default view (mean absolute Laplacian 1.188 against 1.140), so the larger image was not shipped: the softness is the source's.
entries.revisitWhen: A sharper complete source map exists.

entries.subject: Unobserved rows in the OPAL visible map
entries.finding: The map never observed rows 0-35 north of 82.8 degrees, rows 431-444 behind the rings and rows 887-899 south of 87.4 degrees. The rows beside the equatorial mask are ragged or dimmed toward it (rows 430 and 445 average 12 and 8 of 255), so a fill between them stayed black. The geometry recipe names rows 0-35, 426-451 and 887-899; row 425 holds no texel more than 25 % off its row median in any channel and row 452 is within 1 % of the level beyond it. Preparation fills the named rows by linear interpolation in latitude between the rows beside them, detecting nothing from pixel values, and the rotation-B map of the same year has the same gaps so it cannot fill them.
entries.revisitWhen: An OPAL or other global release observes those latitude rows.

entries.subject: NASA Cassini PIA21611 north-polar projection
entries.finding: The 2017 Cassini north-polar map was removed from the default visible body because it produced a visibly separate, cross-mission cap over the 2025 Hubble OPAL map. Both prepared polar caps now project the same OPAL surface after its declared unobserved rows are filled.
entries.revisitWhen: A separate Cassini-era dataset view is requested with a coherent body map and presentation.

entries.subject: Cassini ISS contrast-enhanced global color map of 2011-08-11
entries.finding: A dataset beside the Hubble dates: the PDS bundle's contrast-enhanced RED/GRN/BL1 map (3,601 by 1,801 samples, 0.1 degrees, planetocentric latitude, west longitude; frames at 161 km per pixel). Its three FITS planes hold 8-bit display values. The first stored row is 90 N although the LAT_C card reads -90:0.1:90; stored column c is west longitude 0.1 c degrees although the LON_W card reads 360.0:-0.1:0.0 (raw frame W1691726068_1 correlates 0.62 with the prepared storm band, 0.23 with its mirror); the first stored column is zero on 1,595 of 1,801 rows and is cropped. Rows 0-110, 898-906, 954-1071 and 1721-1800 are zero (17.7 % of the map) and draw the gray grid; rows 919-953 are dimmed by the rings' shadow and shown as archived. No color change is applied.

entries.subject: Cassini's 2011 color map as the default visible body
entries.finding: Measured against the Hubble 2025 map: the fine detail's correlation length along longitude is 0.14 to 0.18 degrees between 20 and 60 N against Hubble's 0.23 to 0.33, and a composed default view at the app's on-screen size held 1.27 times Hubble's fine detail (3.9 times in the contrast-enhanced product). But 17.7 % of the map is blank, and with the shadow-dimmed rows about 21 degrees of latitude around the equator would be an interpolated fill; the values are 8-bit (40 to 57 levels per color in the archive's unenhanced product) and from 2011. The user kept Hubble as the default and took the Cassini map as a dataset, 2026-10-05.
entries.revisitWhen: A calibrated global color map without the ring-shadow band is released.

entries.subject: Cassini UVIS HSP alpha Virginis occultation, 2006 day 285
entries.finding: Ring opacity is the 1 km-bin normal optical depth profile: of 73,713 bins between 66,900 and 140,612 km, 60,886 carry a measured depth, 4,518 are clean bins below the detection floor and count as empty and 8,309 are flagged corrupted and interpolated from neighbours, each becoming a transmission byte of 255 times exp of minus the optical depth; the Encke and Keeler gaps, the Cassini division and the F ring now come from this occultation rather than the retired hand-authored clearings.

entries.subject: Radius-indexed ring color dataset
entries.finding: No qualified radial color dataset exists: the Cassini ISS natural-color ring mosaics in the Photojournal are perspective views rather than radius-indexed strips, so the ring color is uniform white under the declared solar tint.
entries.revisitWhen: A radius-indexed ring color or reflectance profile is released.

entries.subject: Hubble OPAL F225W and FQ889N single-band maps
entries.finding: The ultraviolet and methane datasets use the pinned 1,800 by 900 single-band maps, keeping rotation A intact rather than averaging temporally separated cloud detail with rotation B, filling only unmeasured polar and ring-occluded rows in the same longitude, applying a declared false-color palette and a pansharpening pass clamped to 0.88-1.12 so the Hubble maps keep authority over broad spectral luminance; they are source-backed spectral interpretations, not pure single-band products or natural color.

entries.subject: Hubble WFC3 programme 17843 ring frames of 2025-08-29
entries.finding: The ultraviolet, methane and thermal ring images recolored the UVIS profile with hand-set per-ring gains that were only compared by eye with ifcu37ccq (F225W), ifcu37cdq (F631N) and ifcu37ceq (FQ889N); no ring brightness was measured from those frames, so the images were removed and every dataset shows the one measured ring profile.
entries.revisitWhen: Ring I/F per ring region is measured from the programme 17843 frames, or a published ring spectrum covers 225 nm and 889 nm.

entries.subject: Replacement profiles for the D, G and E rings
entries.finding: The UVIS occultation covers 66,900 to 140,612 km; the D ring inside it and the G and E rings outside it are not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: A dataset resolves complete D, G and E ring profiles.

entries.subject: Thermal view as an explicit illustration
entries.finding: The thermal view was schematic: visible luminance, cloud-window contrast and authored latitude and longitude patterns under an orange palette, with no detector samples. It was removed.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered global thermal or brightness-temperature map of Saturn is qualified.

entries.subject: Cassini VIMS high-contrast infrared scan PIA17468
entries.finding: The scan was considered as a physical reference but is a narrow observed swath in a particular viewing geometry, not a registered global thermal map suitable for this globe, so it remains a reference rather than a texture input.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered global infrared map suitable for this globe is released.

entries.subject: Global CIRS temperature map
entries.finding: The existing sources do not qualify a global CIRS temperature map; the README records it as unresolved rather than claiming such a dataset does not exist.
entries.revisitWhen: A qualified global CIRS temperature map is located or released.

entries.subject: Mankovich and Fuller (2021) diffuse-core result and Movshovitz density profiles
entries.finding: The interior radial presentation follows the 2021 ring-seismology diffuse-core interpretation, which places the stable core-envelope transition out to about 60 percent of Saturn's radius, cross-checked against the CC0 Movshovitz density profiles, with composition and terminology checked against the NASA/JPL-Caltech interior cutaway illustration and no pixels from it redistributed; the visible radii and colors are declared presentation choices, not hard boundaries or measured colors.

entries.subject: One schematic bank for the interior layers
entries.finding: The structural section, metallic-hydrogen and diffuse-core textures share one schematic bank because none of the observation datasets measures below Saturn's atmosphere, and the declared false-color responses of the other datasets do not recolor the unobserved deep layers.

entries.subject: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Saturn ring statistics
entries.finding: The published PDS boundaries constrain the Cassini and Roche divisions, the Encke and Keeler gaps and the F ring, whose 140,224 km core uses the PDS optical-depth range rather than a painted line; the prepared image extends through the F ring's 140,612 km outer boundary. Nothing is drawn inside the profile's first radius, 66,900 km.

entries.subject: Prepared opacity and extrema emphasis in the rings
entries.finding: Twenty-nine named narrow features (5 dark gaps and 24 bright hairlines, among them the Encke and Keeler gaps and the F-ring core) get a minimum width of 4 texels at density 1 and 6 at density 2; bright hairlines also take an opacity gain of 1.8, or 1.35 at half scale for 21 of them. Source radii and the rest of the profile are unchanged. The C-ring alpha remap described earlier is no longer in the recipe.

entries.subject: IAU radii, SAT441 kernel and the prepared time scale
entries.finding: The recipe states radii of 60,268, 60,268 and 54,364 km from NAIF pck00011.tpc with the ring plane bound to sat441.bsp, and motion uses NASA's ring-seismology interior rotation of 10 h 33 min 38 s mapped to 72 visual seconds for a 528.027778 acceleration shared by body and rings, with each ring group's circular period from SAT441's GM; the cloud-top period spread across latitude bands is an explicit presentation model, not a claim that NASA specifies a continuous wind law.

entries.subject: Prepared 5,772 K solar color multiplier
entries.finding: The #fff1ea multiplier is derived from a 5,772 K Planck distribution, taken from NASA's Sun fact sheet, through the CIE 1931 observer and linear sRGB/D65 normalized by its maximum channel and multiplied into the surface texels once during preparation; the README calls it a declared colorimetric display approximation, not flat white light or a full spectral renderer.

entries.subject: Lambert illumination parameters adapted from the OpenSpace globe shader
entries.finding: The Lambert parameters adapted from the OpenSpace globe shader were replaced by the OPAL Minnaert laws of the map.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Prepared reciprocal ring and body shadows
entries.finding: One prepared world-light vector drives both shadows: Saturn's shadow on the rings is cast with four subpixel rays per ring texel against the oblate ellipsoid and emitted as a separate alpha overlay with a 0.16 transmission floor, and the rings' shadow on Saturn samples the actual prepared radial ring alpha so source gaps and density bands survive; both are cross-checked against NASA photojournal references and form one prepared presentation state, not a date-specific simulation.

entries.subject: Retained three-storm weather snapshot
entries.finding: The earlier default presentation pasted a checked 290 by 34 static snapshot, prepared from OpenSpace surface texels and three authored storm kernels, over nine visible-color body faces. It was an artistic presentation rather than scientific storm data and has been removed from the selected dataset and runtime asset closure.
entries.revisitWhen: A distinct, explicitly labeled artistic-storm dataset is requested; it must remain off by default and separate from observation products.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator model of 2026-08-29
entries.finding: The sidebar spectrum is a prepared 253-sample disk-reflectance model covering 0.35 to 1.0 micrometres at R=240 reporting I/F apparent albedo, and the temperature-pressure chart reads the checked 60-layer profile from the same expanded configuration over its full 10 bar to 2 nanobar range; both requests are recorded in the shared acquisition plan.

entries.subject: JPL satellite catalogue of 293 Saturn moons
entries.finding: The retained catalogue records the 293 moons listed by JPL on 2026-08-29, with mean elements for 291, S/2009 S1's published approximate ring-moonlet orbit and S/2009 S2's orbital radius from MPEC 2026-M19 without committing the circular text. Forty-six moons have their own object packages; the 245 others with a Horizons code are drawn as plain dots at their Horizons positions by the saturn-minor-moons package, and the two without an ephemeris are not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: The shared runtime gains a contract for rendering a moon system inside a planet scene.

entries.subject: Dated test or browser run for this record
entries.finding: The README's evidence section records a browser run of 2026-10-05: the default view in headless Chrome with a GPU at 2x pixel density, on css.earth v0.6524 and on the version that changed the limb, measured on the same rays, with the before-and-after image it displays.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hubble OPAL's Minnaert coefficients, the correction OPAL removed before projection, put back relative to the flood-lit disc centre, one law per display channel: red 0.798, green 0.698, blue 0.728. Each is the README's coefficients weighted by the light the channel shows; see display-channel-limb-law. Each channel took its nearest filter (0.80, 0.65, 0.86) from 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-05, and blue took F395N's 0.40 before that; see opal-f467m-blue-limb.

entries.subject: Authored limb lighting: pearl-blue limb color, Oren-Nayar term, 0.05 ambient and smoothstep terminator adapted from OpenSpace
entries.finding: Replaced by the OPAL Minnaert laws of the map.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Color tie of the OPAL visible map to Karkoschka's 1995 whole-disc spectrum
entries.finding: The OPAL color TIF is arbitrarily scaled per channel and rendered 1.4 times too blue (map mean blue/red 0.65 in linear light). Karkoschka's full-disc albedo of Saturn (phase 5.7 degrees, rings edge-on, PDS 1995LOW.TAB) times a 5,772 K Planck spectrum through the CIE 1931 observer gives linear sRGB 0.6168, 0.4713, 0.2982 (#ceb794), green/red 0.7640 and blue/red 0.4834. Divided by the limb law's disc means (0.7706, 0.8350, 0.8146) the map targets are green/red 0.7052 and blue/red 0.4573; the solar-tinted map measured 0.9317 and 0.6975 (cosine-weighted, linear), so the gains are red 1, green 0.7569, blue 0.6556. With the nearest-filter law of 2026-09-25 the targets were 0.6759 and 0.5057. The swatch's independent Payne et al. (2026) spectrum agrees under a D65 white: green/red 0.863 and blue/red 0.589 against Karkoschka's 0.863 and 0.593.

entries.subject: Tying the map's own mean color, rather than the lit disc, to Karkoschka's whole-disc color
entries.finding: Karkoschka measured the disc with its limb darkening; OPAL divided each filter's darkening out and the overlay puts it back per channel, so a map mean tied straight to the whole-disc ratios (gains green 0.824, blue 0.6952) renders a disc of green/red 0.856 instead of 0.764 and an olive limb (a* -5 at 0.85-0.95 of the radius) in a preview built with the lane's own surface and limb code.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing while the lighting overlay puts back a per-channel limb law.

entries.subject: One README filter per display channel: F631N, F502N and F467M
entries.finding: From 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-05 each display channel took the README filter nearest its primary: red F631N 0.80, green F502N 0.65, blue F467M 0.86 ("F467M 0.86 .00507"; before that blue took F395N's 0.40 and the limb turned gray-blue, b* -16 at the rim). Green then darkened least and the limb turned olive: on css.earth v0.6524 the default view's green/red ratio rose from 0.78, 200 pixels inside the edge, to 1.02, 5 pixels inside, where Jupiter's goes from 0.87 to 0.91. No single filter is a channel's law; see display-channel-limb-law.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: a channel's law is weighted over the wavelengths it shows.

entries.subject: Limb law of each display channel, weighted over the README's filters
entries.finding: The README gives one Minnaert coefficient per filter (F395N 0.40, F467M 0.86, F502N 0.65, F631N 0.80, F763M 0.85); a display channel shows a range of wavelengths. Each channel's flood-lit profile is the sum of mu^(2k - 1) over 380-780 nm, k interpolated in wavelength between filters and held outside them (a join that is ours), weighted by Saturn's albedo (1995LOW.TAB) times a 5,772 K Planck spectrum through the CIE 1931 observer into linear sRGB; the same spectrum reproduces the whole-disc color record. The methane-band filters FQ727N and FQ889N are left out. The Minnaert exponents that fit those profiles over the disc out to 86.3 degrees are red 0.798, green 0.698 and blue 0.728, departing from the profiles by at most 0.004, 0.0001 and 0.028. At 0.95 of the radius green/red is 1.26 times its centre value and blue/red 1.18 (1.42 and 0.87 with one filter per channel): the limb pales instead of turning olive. On screen, 5 pixels inside the edge of the default view, green/red went from 1.02 to 0.89 and blue/red from 0.55 to 0.66 (2026-10-05).

entries.subject: Dark dashes along the limb of the flood-lit overlay
entries.finding: Under flood light the lane floored a grazing texel's emission at one texel (1/256) but not its incidence, so the limb law was held at the edge of its data on the emission alone and fell to about 2 % of the centre on scattered texels of the outermost ring: alpha up to 235 where the held law gives 136. At 8 screen pixels per texel they read as dark dashes: 29 dark dips along 32 degrees of limb on css.earth v0.6524 at 2x pixel density, none on Jupiter. Serving the frame with those 462 texels capped at 136 left 4 dips, and hiding the overlay showed the dashes were not the body's seams (more overlap between faces changed nothing). The lane now holds the incidence with the emission under flood light: 3 dips on the same rays, 2026-10-05. The overlay's color past the silhouette is also kept by each texel's share inside (4 x 4 samples); that alone left the count at 31.

entries.subject: Brightness of the color-tied visible map
entries.finding: The tie keeps red and lowers green and blue, so the map loses cosine-weighted luminance (0.426 to 0.337 with the law of 2026-09-25) and Saturn looked brown in the app (whole-disc Y 0.315 against 0.409 on main). The tied map gets back its untied mean luminance with one factor on all three channels, 1.239 (1.264 on 2026-09-25, 1.269 after the ring-hidden rows were refilled), then a soft shoulder, 0.8 + 0.2 (1 - exp(-(m - 0.8) / 0.2)), on each texel's brightest channel, all channels by the same amount: 5.22 % of texels, none clipped, ratios kept. Chosen by the user on a preview built with the lane's own code, 2026-09-25.

entries.subject: Dated Hubble OPAL visible-color sequence (8 rotations)
entries.finding: One publisher RGB composite per included cycle, component FITS coverage, source-backed map frame and observation dates. Gray grid preserves missing coverage. Current scene lighting and rings remain a presentation, not the historical observing geometry. See the Hubble dates section of the README.
